newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades mostly steady.

text.p: German call money rates traded mostly steady on Friday between 2.975/3.05 percent, with dealers saying rates could come off slightly in afternoon trading as banks try to unload funds before the weekend.
The bulk of trades was conducted at three percent after overnight funds traded between 3.00/3.05 percent on Thursday.

This afternoon rates however may trend slightly lower again after banks know more about their reserve holdings at the Bundesbank and may be eager to unload excess funds ahead of the weekend, dealers added.
But looking ahead, money market rates are largely expected to trade around the three percent repo rate in the coming week, barring any rate swings associated with month-end trading, dealers said.
Time deposits traded steady to slightly lower, dealers said, with three-month rates quoted around 3.03/3.08 percent.

Banks holdings at the Bundesbank stood at 37.1 billion marks on Thursday compared with 37.9 billion marks on Wednesday with the monthly average remaining unchanged at 38.6 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were negligible on Thursday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.05100 percent on Friday compared with 3.03400 percent on Thursday.
